RapWire 24/7: Jay-Z, Erykah Badu, Young Nudy, Drake and Don Toliver, and DistroKid.

@Rapwire247
caption:
1) Jay-Z’s three-night JAŸ-Z30 run at Yankee Stadium generated $42,290,766 from 136,934 tickets sold, according to box-office figures attributed to Touring Data. The July 10–12 shows celebrated the 30th anniversary of “Reasonable Doubt” and the 25th anniversary of “The Blueprint,” turning a Bronx homecoming into a new rap-concert benchmark.

2) Erykah Badu canceled five October European performances in Paris, Milan, Sofia and Katowice, citing unforeseen circumstances. Her London, Amsterdam, Brussels and Basel dates remain on the published itinerary, and affected fans were told to follow local ticketing guidance. @erykahbadu

3) Young Nudy’s next project, “Just Doin Me,” is listed for Oct. 28, with “Who Dat Is” serving as the rollout’s lead single. Apple Music currently shows a 17-song pre-release page while other coverage cites a 19-song listing, so the final track count is still moving. @youngnudy

4) Drake and Don Toliver’s “Solar Eclipse” now has an official music video, released alongside “Cold Shoulder” from the FOMO rollout. Complex reports that both songs first appeared in Drake’s short film before arriving on the expanded “HABIBTI (FOMO)” edition, and Apple Music lists the standalone visual. @champagnepapi @dontoliver

5) DistroKid confirmed to The Verge that a small number of recordings were removed in response to claims made by Universal Music Group, while saying it disputes the label’s lawsuit. Artists have reported missing releases and little notice or recourse, and the federal case remains allegations rather than a ruling. The dispute matters because a distributor’s enforcement choices can take independent music offline before a court decides the underlying claims.

@Rapwire247
